definitions: Used to add a proviso or a qualification to something previously said.
Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or modifies what has just been said.
Used to emphasize a point or to draw attention to an important detail.
examples: It was a tough game, mind you, we played well.
He's very clever, mind you, he can be a bit arrogant.
I don't usually like spicy food, mind you, this is delicious.
